polityNote: Azerbaijan from the dissolution of the USSR (26 Dec 1991) to the eve of Kangarli rayon (19 Mar 2004), from which the present-day record carries the rayons back. First-level units as the CIA World Factbook (US BGN) lists them 1995-2003: 59 rayons, 11 cities of republican subordination and the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic as ONE unit (its rayons are subordinate to it, so the 2004 split of Babek and Sharur does not move a first-level line). Atoms: geoBoundaries AZE ADM2 (2020, traced from Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 3.0; 79 polygons, 11,130 vertices — 2.5 times Natural Earth's 4,516). A rayon is drawn as its 2020 atom because no rayon line outside the war zone moved 1991-2020 except Samukh (organised 18 Feb 1992 from Khanlar; withheld before) and Kangarli (inside the AR). Under the rule 'drawn only where Azerbaijan administered it': Khankendi and, after the ceasefire of 12 May 1994, the wholly occupied Lachin, Kalbajar, Qubadli, Zangilan, Khojaly, Khojavend and Shusha rayons and Shusha city are atomsOutside; the partly occupied Agdam, Tartar, Fuzuli, Jabrayil and Goranboy, and every war-zone rayon while the front moved (1991-1994), are unresolved because the line of contact is not an atom line. The era map (CShapes) places all of this ground in Azerbaijan; the split follows administration, not the map. Small exclaves held by the other side (Karki in the Sadarak atom, the Qazakh exclaves) cannot be separated from their atoms and are drawn with them. Check 1 (2026-10-06): the AR's union vs OpenHistoricalMap's Naxçıvan MR IoU 0.953 and vs geoBoundaries' OpenStreetMap ADM1 0.942 (Natural Earth 0.881); rayon by rayon the atoms agree with Natural Earth only at median IoU 0.73 (pooled 0.757), and the city atoms are undersized against published areas (Ganja 38.5 km2 vs 110, Mingachevir 44 vs 130), so lines between rayons are only as good as the Wikipedia trace.

sources.title: Vikipediya — Ağdərə rayonu (oldid 8901604)
sources.says: Agdara rayon (the former Mardakert raion) was abolished by Milli Majlis decision No. 327 of 13 Oct 1992 and its territory divided among Agdam, Kalbajar and Tartar.

sources.title: Wikipedia — Kalbajar District (oldid 1376270961)
sources.says: The district was occupied by Armenian forces on 3 April 1993.

sources.title: Wikipedia — Agdam District (oldid 1374573099)
sources.says: Agdam was occupied on 23 July 1993.

sources.title: Wikipedia — Fuzuli District (oldid 1375883013)
sources.says: The city of Fuzuli was occupied on 23 Aug 1993; Horadiz became the temporary district centre.

sources.title: Wikipedia — Jabrayil District (oldid 1376244559)
sources.says: Occupied on 23 Aug 1993, save the village of Jojug Marjanly, recaptured on 6 Jan 1994.

sources.title: Wikipedia — Zangilan District (oldid 1378491725)
sources.says: The district came under occupation on 29 Oct 1993.

sources.title: Wikipedia — Bishkek Protocol (oldid 1346763433)
sources.says: Ceasefire signed on 12 May 1994; Azerbaijani forces then held Shahumian and the eastern parts of Martakert and Martuni.

sources.title: Wikipedia — Armenian-occupied territories surrounding Nagorno-Karabakh (oldid 1367031690)
sources.says: Before 2020 Kalbajar, Lachin, Qubadli, Zangilan and Jabrayil (except Jojug Marjanly) were occupied in whole, Fuzuli about 33% and Agdam 77%.
